title: Prosecutor v. Dario Kordić and Mario Čerkez (Lašva Valley, Central Bosnia: destruction of mosques and other religious and educational institutions)
body: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY); Trial Chamber III and Appeals Chamber
summary: Dario Kordić and Mario Čerkez, Bosnian Croat figures in the Lašva Valley region of Central Bosnia, were tried together at the ICTY. Among the 44 counts were two for "destruction or damage to religious or educational institutions", described by the Trial Chamber as violations of the laws or customs of war: Count 43 (Kordić) and Count 44 (Čerkez). In the Trial Judgement of 26 February 2001 the Chamber stated that "the HVO deliberately targeted mosques and other religious and educational institutions" as part of a common plan, found Kordić guilty on Count 43 and Čerkez guilty on Count 44, and sentenced them to 25 and 15 years. In the Appeals Judgement of 17 December 2004 the Appeals Chamber affirmed Kordić's Count 43 conviction for Ahmići and Han Ploča-Grahovci but reversed it for Stari Vitez, affirmed his 25-year sentence, and reversed Čerkez's convictions under Count 44, imposing a new sentence of 6 years. The written judgements were not read for this entry, so the entry does not say which buildings were found destroyed.
legal_basis: The ICTY's case information sheet groups the charges of destroying religious or educational buildings under Article 3 of the Statute (violations of the laws or customs of war); the Trial Chamber's pronouncement describes Counts 43 and 44 as "violations of the laws or customs of war (destruction or damage to religious or educational institutions)". As reproduced in a University of Oslo copy of the Statute, Article 3(d) lists "seizure of, destruction or wilful damage done to institutions dedicated to religion, charity and education, the arts and sciences, historic monuments and works of art and science" and Article 3(b) lists "wanton destruction of cities, towns or villages, or devastation not justified by military necessity". The two accused were charged under Article 7(1) (individual responsibility, covering a person who "planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted") and Article 7(3) (responsibility of a superior for acts of subordinates). The Trial Chamber found Kordić not liable under Article 7(3); it found Čerkez liable under Article 7(3) for offences arising from attacks on three locations (Vitez, Stari Vitez and Večeriska). The Appeals Chamber's disposition reversed all of Čerkez's Article 7(3) convictions. The exact Statute article under which Counts 43 and 44 were framed in the indictment and the elements the Chambers applied were not read.
outcome: TRIAL (Trial Judgement, IT-95-14/2-T, 26 February 2001, as pronounced by Trial Chamber III): Count 43 (destruction or damage to religious or educational institutions): Dario Kordić guilty. Count 44 (same offence): Mario Čerkez guilty. The Chamber stated that "the HVO deliberately targeted mosques and other religious and educational institutions", that there was "a pattern of destruction and plunder in all the places attacked by the HVO", and that all this was part of the common plan. Overall sentences: Kordić 25 years' imprisonment, Čerkez 15 years' imprisonment, with time in custody from 6 October 1997 deducted. Kordić was found guilty on Counts 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 10, 12, 21, 22, 38, 39 and 43 and not guilty on Counts 9, 11, 13, 23-28 and 37. Čerkez was found guilty on Counts 2, 5, 6, 14, 15, 17, 19, 29-31, 33, 35, 41, 42 and 44 and not guilty on Counts 16, 18, 20, 32, 34, 36 and 40 (the English transcript's reading of Counts 23-28 was ambiguous; the English press release and the French summary give not guilty). APPEAL (Appeals Judgement, IT-95-14/2-A, 17 December 2004, as pronounced): Kordić: Count 43, "destruction or wilful damage to institutions dedicated to religion or education", affirmed for Ahmići and for Han Ploča-Grahovci, and reversed for Stari Vitez; other convictions were reversed location by location, Count 1 (persecutions) affirmed in part, and the sentence of 25 years affirmed. Čerkez: convictions under Count 44 reversed (for Večeriska, Donja Večeriska and Stari Vitez, and for Vitez); the convictions the pronouncement affirms are under Article 7(1) only, for Counts 2 (persecutions), 29 and 30 relating to the Vitez cinema and SDK building; new sentence of 6 years, enforced immediately under Rule 118; the Appeals press release states that this was less than the time he had already served and that immediate release was ordered. The pronouncement and press releases do not name particular mosques or buildings, and the Appeals Chamber's reasoning on Counts 43 and 44 (including why the Stari Vitez and Čerkez convictions were reversed) was not read.

timeline.title: Initial indictment
timeline.description: The ICTY case information sheet gives 10 November 1995 as the date of the initial indictment (IT-95-14/2, "Lašva Valley"). The amended indictment is dated 30 September 1998.

timeline.title: Both accused transferred to the Tribunal
timeline.description: The case information sheet records the arrest and transfer of both accused on 6 October 1997; they pleaded not guilty at their initial appearance on 8 October 1997.

timeline.title: Amended indictment
timeline.description: The case information sheet gives 30 September 1998 as the date of the amended indictment. The Trial Judgement press release states that the Indictment contains 44 counts; the counts relevant here are 43 (Kordić) and 44 (Čerkez), described in the Trial Chamber's pronouncement as violations of the laws or customs of war (destruction or damage to religious or educational institutions).

timeline.title: Trial opens
timeline.description: The trial opened on 12 April 1999; closing arguments were heard on 14 and 15 December 2000.

timeline.title: Trial Judgement
timeline.description: Trial Chamber III found Kordić guilty on Count 43 and Čerkez guilty on Count 44. It also stated that "the HVO deliberately targeted mosques and other religious and educational institutions". Sentences: Kordić 25 years, Čerkez 15 years. Judgement reference IT-95-14/2-T.

timeline.title: Notices of appeal filed
timeline.description: The case information sheet gives 12 March 2001 (defence) and 13 March 2001 (Prosecution) as the dates of the notices of appeal.

timeline.title: Appeal hearings
timeline.description: The Appeals Chamber heard the appeals on 17, 18 and 19 May 2004. Final deliberations took place on 2 December 2004.

timeline.title: Appeals Judgement
timeline.description: For Kordić, the Appeals Chamber affirmed Count 43 for Ahmići and for Han Ploča-Grahovci, reversed Count 43 for Stari Vitez, and affirmed the 25-year sentence. For Čerkez, it reversed his convictions under Count 44 (for Veceriska, Donja Veceriska, Stari Vitez and for Vitez) and imposed a new sentence of 6 years. Judgement reference IT-95-14/2-A.

timeline.title: Kordić transferred to Austria
timeline.description: Kordić was transferred to Austria on 8 June 2006 to serve his 25-year sentence.

changelog.change: Initial draft. Known gaps: (1) the written Trial Judgement and written Appeal Judgement were NOT read (refworld PDFs and unhcr archive copies were blocked or behind verification pages; curl to icty.org was blocked), so the entry rests on the Chambers' oral pronouncements/transcripts and ICTY press releases; consequently which mosques/buildings were found destroyed, the elements applied, and the Appeals Chamber's reasons for reversing Kordić's Stari Vitez conviction and Čerkez's Count 44 convictions are not stated; (2) the ICTY consolidated Statute PDF was blocked; Articles 3(b), 3(d), 7(1), 7(3) were seen only as truncated excerpts in a University of Oslo reproduction; (3) the English case information sheet was not opened (French one read); the exact Statute article of Counts 43/44 in the indictment was not seen; (4) all pages were read via a fetch tool that summarises content, so quotations and the lists of counts must be re-verified against the originals before approval; (5) the Appeals hearing transcript of 17 May 2004 was only partly read (first 100,000 characters) and is not cited; (6) a Frulli article (Italian Yearbook of International Law XV, 2005) was opened but says little about this case and is not cited; no attributable analysis was found, so interpretation is null; (7) Croatia is not linked as no read source states a state role; the Trial Chamber's finding concerned the Bosnian Croat leadership and HVO, and its wording on a common plan was taken only from the oral summary. Heritage relevance: the counts concern religious and educational buildings generally, not named World Heritage sites.

Verification against the fetched sources. All counts of conviction/acquittal per accused, Counts 43 (Kordić) and 44 (Čerkez), sentences (trial 25/15 years; appeal 25 affirmed / new 6 years for Čerkez), appeal outcomes by location and trial/appeal separation were confirmed as stated. Fixes: (1) 1998-09-30 timeline event wrongly attributed the 44-count statement to an Appeals hearing transcript of 17 May 2004 (not a cited source) and to src_01; now attributed to the Trial Judgement press release (src_02); (2) removed src_08 (2006 transfer release) from the initial-indictment event, which it does not support; (3) appeal-hearing event: removed the unsupported 'transcript dated 17 May 2004 exists' and the incorrect statement that days came only from the press release, citing src_04 and src_05 for 17-19 May and 2 December 2004; (4) legal_basis: completed the truncated Article 3(d) quotation and removed the 'full text of Article 7(1)/(3) not read' gap, since the Oslo copy shows both articles in full. Not verified: written judgements not opened, so reasoning, named buildings and the exact indictment article for Counts 43/44 remain unstated; pages were read through a summarising fetch tool. Note the case information sheet's 2 December 2004 release date for Čerkez is unexplained and not used.
